title: Build a live race, anywhere
description: A platform for building live mission races with real stations, navigation on the phone and automatic scoring. Outdoors, at home or at a party. No judges, no paper, no chasing everyone around.
tagline: A live race for any group
headline: The live race your team will remember
subhead: Outdoors, at home or at a party, everyone plays the same way. You build the stations, the phone handles the navigation, and the scoring sorts itself out. You keep the part you started for.
primaryAction: Build your first race in 5 minutes
heroTrust: 100% of players stayed active across the first games. Nobody sat it out.
heroChallenge: Would your team have found this station in 60 seconds?
lowFrictionNote: No signup, no card. A live try in 30 seconds.
videoBody: I am Ahiya, 17, from Jerusalem. I built RushPoint after trying to run a real mission race and watching how fast it fell apart. Ninety seconds and you will get the idea.

hero.alt: Ahiya Savir explains what RushPoint is and how to build a mission race with it
hero.caption: Ninety seconds: how RushPoint turns any space, from a living room to a neighbourhood, into a live race

missions.title: The tree worth the most points
missions.prompt: Find the tree marked on your map, and get the whole team in frame beside it.

missions.title: The treasure in the house
missions.prompt: Each clue leads to the next room. The last one hides under something soft.

featuresTitle: The hard parts now happen on their own
featuresSubtitle: Almost every team race that falls apart falls apart on logistics rather than on the idea. Everything I learned the hard way is already solved here.

features.title: Automatic scoring
features.description: Answers are checked on the server the moment they are sent. Nobody has to stand at a station, and nobody argues afterwards about who got what.

features.title: With a map or without one
features.description: A mission can be tied to a place, where arriving is verified against the device GPS, or free of one and solvable from anywhere. The same race works in a neighbourhood and in a living room.

features.title: Smart routing between teams
features.description: Each team is sent to a station that is free and close to it. Instead of a queue at one stop, everyone keeps moving.

features.title: Survives a bad signal
features.description: The app is built for open ground: it holds its state, keeps working, and syncs when reception comes back.

features.title: Live control while you run it
features.description: One console shows where every team is, who is stuck and who is ahead. Send a message, close a station or adjust a score without stopping the game.

features.title: Joining takes no install
features.description: Players open a link and type a code. Nothing to download, nothing to sign up for, no passwords forgotten at the worst moment.

stepsTitle: From an idea to teams racing

steps.title: Design the route
steps.description: Drop stations on the map and write a task for each one. Start from a ready made game and change it, or let the system compose one for the occasion.

steps.title: Launch and share a code
steps.description: Press launch and you get a join code. Send it to the group and that is the setup done.

steps.title: Watch it happen
steps.description: Teams start moving, scores update themselves, and you follow all of it on one screen until the finish.

ctaTitle: Your first game is about half an hour away
ctaSubtitle: No card needed. Start from a ready made game and change it, and if something is missing, write to me.

tryMission.title: Actually, play it yourself
tryMission.subtitle: Three real missions, exactly the kinds your teams get in a race. The clock runs, the scoring happens on its own, and at the end you see the screen your players see.
tryMission.startBody: Three missions. Most people finish in about a minute. The faster you solve them, the more points you get, exactly like the real thing.
tryMission.wrongFeedback: Not quite. Try again. A wrong answer costs you time, not points.
tryMission.doneBody: This is exactly what a team sees when they finish: score, time, and where they landed. Nobody sat there with a clipboard. Your next game can be built and run completely for free.
tryMission.doneAction: Let's build you a game for free
tryMission.boardNote: The other teams on this board are illustrative. Your score and your time are entirely real.

occasion.title: What are you building a game for?
occasion.prompt: So we know how to help you. Pick whatever fits best.

missionIdeas.title: Not sure what your teams would do? Start here
missionIdeas.subtitle: The hard part is not the software, it is the blank page. Pick the occasion and the place, and get three real missions you can use exactly as they are.
missionIdeas.note: Take these and run a game on paper if you like. They are yours.

ideas.text: Recreate an old photo of the guest of honour, same pose, whole team in frame.
Letters are hidden on the sign at the entrance. Arrange them into one word and send it.
Find the oldest tree in the park and send your estimate of its age. Closest wins.
Find someone who has lived here over twenty years and ask for one story about the street. Record it.
Put the five places on the list in the order they were built, earliest first.
Shoot a twenty second advert for the spot you are standing in. Everyone appears in it.
How many steps are in the main staircase? Send a number. There is a tolerance.
Buy something sweet nobody on the team has tried before, and film the first bite.
Who is this street named after, and in what year? Two answers, both must be right.
Build a tower from things you find on the ground, buying nothing. Photograph it standing.
Get the whole team across the square without stepping on the paving lines. Film the attempt.
Stand still for one minute and record. Then list three sounds you identified.
Get to the point marked on the map. There is no clue beyond the location itself.
Find one stranger willing to be photographed with you, holding your team sign.
Study the shop window for thirty seconds, walk away, and list every item you remember.
Another team is near you. Photograph both teams together. You both score.
The code for the next station is written on something green within fifty metres. Find it.
One of you gives a thirty second toast to the guest of honour, in public. Film it.

gamePlanner.tagline: The sum nobody does in advance
gamePlanner.title: How many stations do you actually need?
gamePlanner.subtitle: A team race’s ceiling is not the software, it is how many teams can be at a mission at once. Move the sliders and see.

fieldLabels.capacity: Teams at one station at once

gamePlanner.stationsLabel: separate stations needed to finish in time
gamePlanner.verdictOk: This works. The number of stations is reasonable next to the number of missions you planned.
gamePlanner.verdictTight: This is tight. You need more stations than is reasonable to build. Add time, cut missions per team, or let more teams share a station.
gamePlanner.note: A plain capacity sum: each station clears its team count divided by the mission length. A real game also has walking between stations, so treat this as a floor rather than a ceiling.

faqTitle: The questions people ask before they start

faqs.title: Do players need to install an app?
faqs.description: No. Players open a link in their phone browser and start. No app store, no signup, no password. Anyone who wants to can add it to their home screen, but nobody has to.

faqs.title: What happens where there is no signal?
faqs.description: The app keeps working. It holds the state on the device, shows that the connection is gone, and syncs the moment it returns. Missions that do not need a location can be solved offline.

faqs.title: What does it cost?
faqs.description: Playing is free. You can run a real game with real teams without paying and without leaving payment details.

faqs.title: How many teams can I run?
faqs.description: A free run is capped at one hundred participants. If you are planning more than that, it is worth checking in advance rather than on the day.

faqs.title: Who scores the missions?
faqs.description: The server. Time, location and answers are checked automatically and the board updates within seconds. Photo and video missions are the only ones that wait for a person, and you can set those to approve themselves too.

faqs.title: How do I know where the teams are?
faqs.description: There is a live console with a map, a table, distress alerts and a chat with each team. You can pause a station mid game, award a bonus, or skip one mission for one team without touching anyone else.

faqs.title: What about safety with children?
faqs.description: You can draw an allowed area and the system flags a team that leaves it. There is a distress button that reaches staff with the location attached. There is also a guardian consent step for groups that need one.

faqs.title: How long does it take to build a game?
faqs.description: A sensible first game takes about half an hour. You can also start from a ready template and edit it, or answer a few questions about your event and let the system assemble one for you.
